title: Return browser-rendered image bytes
objective: Add browser Plotly export capability discovery and PNG/SVG/JPEG/WebP byte-return APIs with safe data-URL decoding, types, accessibility-neutral cleanup, and focused unit/browser tests

oracles: Pure data URL unit vectors and real Chromium Plotly export smoke tests

validation: node_modules/.bin/tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --skipLibCheck --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --target es2022 --lib es2022,dom packages/flint-wasm/plotly-renderer.d.ts

runs.command: node_modules/.bin/tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --skipLibCheck --module nodenext --moduleResolution nodenext --target es2022 --lib es2022,dom packages/flint-wasm/plotly-renderer.d.ts

handoff.summary: Added browser Plotly export capability discovery and a Uint8Array image API for PNG, JPEG, WebP, and SVG. The decoder handles strict base64, percent-escaped base64, and byte-preserving percent-encoded payloads without Node-only Buffer APIs. Focused tests cover formats, malformed data, default PNG behavior, and cleanup; the existing Chromium smoke now verifies real Plotly PNG bytes.
risks: The full browser-smoke command could not run locally because the pre-existing flint-wasm build expects an imported-module cache file that the current compiler no longer writes at that path; an ad hoc real Chromium plus bundled Plotly check passed with the PNG signature.

The broad integration and changed-files gates require native FLINT/FFLAS build products absent from this worktree and fail in unrelated native arithmetic tests before providing a useful renderer signal.
Decoded image output necessarily allocates a Uint8Array in addition to Plotly's data URL; a future higher-level export service should enforce output-size limits.
next_steps: Integration should expose browserGraphicsExportCapabilities and sageDisplayToImageBytes through the planned higher-level export_capabilities/browser-to-kernel bridge without changing these low-level APIs.
Run packages/flint-wasm/test/browser-smoke.mjs in a fully provisioned CoWasm browser CI environment on Linux and Windows.
